theme: Amaziah, Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, mixed faithfulness
readingInstruction: Read 2 Chronicles 25:1-28:27. Amaziah, Uzziah, Jotham, and Ahaz take the throne in turn. Look for the word “strong,” and for what happens when strength leads to pride.
settingTheScene: These four kings cover about 100 years. Amaziah starts well and ends with idolatry. Uzziah is one of the most successful kings, but he oversteps in the temple and is struck with leprosy. Jotham is faithful. Ahaz is among the worst, closing the temple and sacrificing his own children. Isaiah’s early ministry takes place in this period, which you read in Unit 12.
observation: “And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not with a whole heart” (25:2).
“The LORD is able to give you much more than this” (25:9).
“And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD… And as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper” (26:4-5).
“And his fame spread far, for he was marvelously helped, till he was strong” (26:15).
“But when he was strong, he grew proud, to his destruction” (26:16).
“So Jotham became mighty, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God” (27:6).
“For the LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had made Judah act sinfully” (28:19).
“In the time of his distress he became yet more faithless to the LORD” (28:22).
interpretation:
Amaziah’s description is chilling: he did what was right, “yet not with a whole heart.” He listens to a prophet when it costs him money, dismissing 100,000 hired soldiers from Israel because “the LORD is able to give you much more than this.” But after defeating Edom, he brings home their gods and worships them. When a prophet confronts him, he threatens the prophet. A partial faith ends in ruin.

Uzziah’s story is the most important in this section. He reigned for 52 years and “as long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.” He built towers, dug cisterns, organized a large army, and developed new weapons. His fame spread. “He was marvelously helped, till he was strong.” And then the dangerous line: “But when he was strong, he grew proud, to his destruction.” He went into the temple to burn incense, which was the priest’s job. When eighty priests confronted him, he raged. And leprosy broke out on his forehead. He lived in isolation the rest of his life. The point is stark: success, apart from humility, destroys. This is the same Uzziah in whose death year Isaiah saw the LORD (Isaiah 6:1).

Jotham is a quiet counterexample. “He ordered his ways before the LORD his God.” The word “ordered” means to establish firmly. No dramatic event, just steady faithfulness, and he “became mighty.”

Ahaz is the opposite: he made metal images for Baals, burned his children, and shut the temple doors. When Assyria pressed him, he sent them the temple treasures. Verse 22 says, “In the time of his distress he became yet more faithless.” Hardship should drive us to God. For Ahaz it drove him away.
connection: Proverbs 16:18: “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.” James 4:6: God gives grace to the humble. Luke 18:14: “Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled.” Isaiah 6:1-5 records the vision that came in the year Uzziah died. Hebrews 7:26-27 says Jesus is the high priest we need. Romans 12:3: do not think of yourself more highly than you ought.
application:
Ask whether any success in your life has made you less dependent on God.

Be like Jotham: order your ways before the LORD, steadily and quietly.

Notice where you are serving God “not with a whole heart,” and ask him to unify your heart.
prayerPrompts: Ask God for a whole heart.
Ask him to keep you humble when you are strong.
Ask him to drive you to him, not away, when you are distressed.
